summary: Afghanistan is the number one producer of opium in the world—responsible for 87% of all illicit opium production—and its opium production has accelerated since the coalition invasion in 2001, with UNODC annual reports showing increases each year. The UNODC's 2004 report showed a 64% increase over the previous year in the area under opium production and a 22% rise in export value to US$2.8 billion, described as "disheartening" and estimating Afghanistan now produces three-fourths of the world's opium and that revenues from growing and trafficking equal half of Afghanistan's gross domestic product. Antonio Maria Costa, executive director of UNODC, said in 2003 it "could be brought under control with a good dose of law enforcement, which at the moment is lacking," and Doug Wankel, Counter Narcotics Coordinator at the U.S. Embassy in Kabul, told USA Today the opium industry is financing terrorism, "subversive activities" and "warlordism" and is a direct threat to the Afghan government and to the national security interests of the United States.
